subject: MAP: slab structure proposal + milestone escrow idea
body:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Brooks <jared.brooks@acme.ai>; Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: slab structure proposal + milestone escrow idea

Hi Jared — attaching an updated slab proposal and a short MAP playbook for the POC -> onramp. High level: we think structuring the commitment in three slabs tied to MAP checkpoints keeps your internal finance comfortable while letting you realize cost savings as you ramp.

Key points in the attachment (MAP_SLA_v2.pdf + pricing_slabs_v3.xlsx):
- Slab 1 (POC, 30 days): 25k token commit, 20% off list for the slab; acceptance = functional eval + latency within 20% of demo numbers.
- Slab 2 (Pilot ramp, next 60 days): additional 100k token commit, 30% off list for slab 2 once acceptance criteria met.
- Slab 3 (Scale ramped commit, 6 months): larger committed volume with step-down pricing and quarterly true-ups.

Escrow idea: to bridge Acme's procurement needs and our desire for predictable onramp, we propose a small financial holdback: 10% of Slab 2 payment goes into a neutral escrow that releases against signed MAP checkpoints (acceptance sign-off + short performance run). This avoids large up-front credits but protects both sides.

Asks:
- Can you confirm procurement/legal would accept an escrow arrangement (we can use a standard third-party vendor)?
- Any internal KPIs beyond latency and functional eval you want included in the MAP acceptance checklist?
- If we get sign-off, we can produce a DocuSign-ready statement of work and the tranche invoice schedule.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

—
Marcus Lin
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
m: (415) 555-0123
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachment: MAP_SLA_v2.pdf (doc stub)
Attachment: pricing_slabs_v3.xlsx (xls stub)

----
From: Jared Brooks <jared.brooks@acme.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>, Lisa Han <lisa.han@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: slab structure proposal + milestone escrow idea

Marcus — thanks for the detailed pack. A few quick clarifying questions from procurement/legal: 

1) Escrow mechanics: who is the escrow agent and can the funds be applied to future invoices if check fails? We prefer that escrow be released to Redwood on pass and returned on fail; applying to future invoices is fine but we need clear triggers.
2) KPI carve-outs: for the POC acceptance, we also need SLOs around inference error rates (we have strict downstream filtering).
3) Do you allow quarterly true-ups or only monthly? Our finance prefers quarterly.

Also, is there any flexibility on the Slab 1 price if we commit to a short trial extension?

Can loop Legal (Lisa) here to do an early read of the escrow clause.

Jared
Head of Platform Partnerships | Acme AI

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: slab structure proposal + milestone escrow idea

Marcus / Priyom — thoughts inline for negotiation posture and concessions: 

- Escrow agent: Suggest using a neutral custodian (Axiom Escrow) — low friction and used in several enterprise deals. We should allow the escrow to apply to future invoices on partial failures but require a return policy window (30 days) on technical remediation.
- KPI additions: add inference error rate (false positives/negatives on our standard eval set) with a tolerance of ±3% for Slab 1; latency SLOs remain primary.
- Billing cadence: agree to quarterly true-ups to match Acme finance preference. This reduces their immediate AP burden and helps us forecast.

Commercial concessions to advance close quickly: 
- Offer a 5% extra credit on first invoice if Acme signs MAP within 10 business days (limited-time incentive).
- If Acme extends POC by 30 days and hits the acceptance checklist, we roll Slab 1 discount to 25% (from 20%) retroactively for that slab.

I attached a clean pricing slab worksheet with suggested invoice dates and an escrow clause bullet we can share with their legal.

- Marissa
Director, Commercial | Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing_slabs_v3.xlsx (xls stub)

----
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Brooks <jared.brooks@acme.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 14:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Revised slab & invoice schedule (v3)

Jared / team — attaching a redlined slab schedule that implements Marissa's recommendations and clarifies escrow triggers. Notes: 

- Escrow agent: Axiom Escrow; funds released on signed checkpoint acceptance; if an acceptance is disputed, a 30-day remediation window before final release.
- Quarterly true-up schedule included; invoices due net-45; tranche dates anchored to MAP sign date.
- Added an early-sign credit (5%) as a one-time invoice credit on slab 1.

I also added a short paragraph defining acceptance evidence: signed acceptance form + 72-hour production run at target latency + sample eval showing error rate within tolerance.

Attachment: pricing_slabs_v3.xlsx (updated)

Thanks — happy to adjust wording if Legal requests changes.

—
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

From: Lisa Han <lisa.han@acme.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jared Brooks <jared.brooks@acme.ai>, Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: slab structure proposal + milestone escrow idea

Marcus / Redwood team — Acme legal has reviewed the proposed escrow language and pricing slabs. We have a few minor redlines (attached) but are supportive of the approach: escrow with Axiom is acceptable; the 30-day remediation window is fine; acceptance evidence clause needs small clarification on which eval dataset is normative.

Next steps from Acme: procurement will issue a PO for Slab 1 net-45, Legal will push the redlines to DocuSign, and platform will run the initial POC as outlined. Please send a DocuSign-ready SOW and we will move to signature this week.

Lisa Han
Senior Counsel | Acme AI

Attachment: Acme_redlines_20260825.pdf (pdf stub)
